# Give the engine e2e tier a CI runner that reports what it covers

## Context

Split from `#17853` so that ticket can stay open on its remaining criterion while the delivered half lands.

`#17853` establishes that the e2e tier runs in no CI workflow — 104 spec files, 60 of them dock or multi-window, executed by nothing. Its six ACs have since been ruled on by its author, @neo-opus-grace ([ruling](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17853#issuecomment-5562777163)): AC-1 amended and met, AC-3 through AC-6 met, and **AC-2 — a classifier path predicate — deferred as a follow-up with a named home**, because building a separate workflow multiplied its cost from two lines inside `test.yml` to either duplicating ~200 lines of classifier or extracting a reusable one. Grace's words: *"#17853 stays open on AC-2. I am not closing it on the merge."*

PR `#18404` therefore cannot carry `Resolves #17853` — merging it would auto-close a ticket both its author and I intend to keep open. This ticket is the leaf that PR actually delivers.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 12 open issues at 2026-09-06T23:06Z; no equivalent. A2A claim sweep over tonight's nightshift: `#18406` (@neo-gpt-emmy), `#18400` (@neo-gpt), `#18401` (@neo-opus-grace) — none on e2e CI wiring.

## The Problem

No workflow calls `playwright.config.e2e.mjs`. Not gated — never called. So an e2e arm's green is *someone ran it by hand once, on some tree*, and an arm can rot for weeks invisibly.

Two structural limits bound what CI can run, both established empirically rather than assumed:

- **GPU** — specs booting the workstation app inherit animated OffscreenCanvas work no hosted runner composites.
- **Time** — @tobiu's ceiling is five minutes of test time, and the full Brain-free set takes 7.2m serial.

A third bounds the reporting: `testIgnore` DESELECTS the Brain-dependent specs rather than skipping them, so a run missing four fifths of the tier still prints `Skipped: 0`. A naive wiring buys a green badge certifying 14 of 104 files with the rest invisible — **a worse false green than the honest absence it replaces.**

## The Fix

A dedicated `E2E (engine tier)` workflow running the canvas-free, build-independent selection serially under `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI=true`, with `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` as the single source for both the invocation and the coverage report so the two cannot describe different populations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A workflow executes e2e specs on `pull_request` and `push` to `dev`.
- [ ] The test step is bounded to five minutes, separately from provisioning.
- [ ] The job summary states the fraction covered and names every excluded population — Brain-deselected, GPU, build-dependent, and selected-but-quarantined — each with an owner.
- [ ] The selection floor fails the job when a path goes stale or an exclusion is undeclared, at the invocation boundary rather than after the runner starts.
- [ ] A controlled `src/` mutation turns the tier red, proving it gates rather than reports.

## Out of Scope

- The classifier path predicate — that is `#17853`'s remaining AC-2, and its correct implementation is a reusable-workflow extraction rather than a second copy of the predicate.
- The Brain-dependent tier (84 files) and the GPU tier (4 files).
- Repairing the excluded and quarantined arms; they carry owners, not fixes, in this delivery.

## Related

- `#17853` — the parent finding, staying open on AC-2.
- PR `#18404` — the delivery.

- 2026-09-06T23:47:32Z @tobiu referenced in commit `60db947` - "ci(test): the engine e2e tier gets a runner, and the badge names what it covers (#18408) (#18404)

* test(workstation): the overflow-cap arm reports its condition instead of aborting (#17853)

The arm died on `getComputedStyle: parameter 1 is not of type 'Element'` — an
abort inside `page.evaluate` that names no condition. Two descendant lookups in
the `capped` block were unguarded while the `ordinary` branch fifteen lines below
already guarded its own indicator, so the file knew the pattern and applied it to
one branch.

Both now resolve once and report through sentinels: a missing text node reads
`no-text-node` rather than throwing, and a missing indicator reads `null`. The
geometry assertion that consumes the indicator gets an explicit presence check
ahead of it, because otherwise the same crash simply moves one line down into
`Cannot read properties of null`.

The point is not that the arm now passes — it does not. It is that the failure
is legible: with the sentinels in place it reports

    the heavy header must stage a multi-action trailing partition
    Expected: > 1   Received: 1

which is this spec's own documented staging guard firing, not a capping defect.
That is a diagnosis; the TypeError was not.

Found while measuring which e2e specs could be wired into CI. A suite cannot be
quarantined intelligently while its failures are aborts.

* ci(test): the engine e2e tier gets a runner, and the badge names what it covers (#17853)

104 e2e spec files, 60 of them dock or multi-window, executed by zero workflows.
`git grep -l playwright.config.e2e -- '.github/*'` returned nothing: not gated,
never called. So "e2e-certified" has meant "someone ran it by hand once, on some
tree", including for the journeys the dock epics are certified on.

Its own workflow rather than a third suite in `test.yml`, because two constraints
bound what it may ever contain. Specs booting the workstation app inherit five
canvas files and drive animated OffscreenCanvas work CI has no GPU for, so that
tier is out of scope — not skipped, out of scope. And the ceiling is five minutes:
measured serially on an idle machine, this selection runs 3.4m where the full
Brain-free set runs 7.2m. Serial is a measurement, not caution; the tier drives
drag thresholds and geometry, which parallel workers on one runner perturb.

The third constraint bounds the REPORTING, and is the one a reader would be
misled by. `testIgnore` removes the Brain-dependent specs from SELECTION rather
than skipping them, so a run missing four fifths of the tier still prints
`Skipped: 0`. A green check here certifies a genuine but PARTIAL tier, and the
coverage step writes that fraction into the job summary so the badge cannot imply
the whole. It counts what the JOB runs, not what the config selects — the first
version reported the larger number and would have been the exact false green it
exists to prevent.

The splitter-proxy arm is quarantined with a real `test.skip`, because it had
none: the `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` already in that file is a docblock line giving a
local run command. Its guard says "known failure on dev", not "local only" — the
arm dies on `crossing the drag threshold must create a splitter proxy`, reproduced
serially at low load and headed on a real GPU, so it is neither contention nor a
compositor gap. Removing the guard is the fix; skipping buys the time to make one.

49 passed, 0 failed, 3.4m with the guard active.

* ci(test): drop the two specs that need build output, and fix the archaeology marker (#17853)

The first hosted run failed in the way only a hosted run could: 9m17s against 3.4m
locally, with a cluster of 30s timeouts. `rendering/LivePreviewMultiWindow` is
parameterised over Dev, Dist Dev and Dist Prod, and the two Dist environments need
built bundles. My checkout HAS `dist/`, so the suite passed here and could not
have passed there — a local green produced by local build output, which is a false
green no amount of local care would have caught. `portal/LearnLinkRoutingNL`
asserts generated learn content for the same reason.

Both are excluded by path rather than by adding `build-all`, which would spend the
five-minute budget on a build in order to reach two specs. Neither is a product
failure and both belong back in the tier the day the pipeline can afford a build.

The coverage summary follows the same decision: it now reports the build tier as a
third excluded group, so the fraction it prints stays the fraction that ran.

Also: the `ticket-ref-ok` marker has to sit ON the ref's line, not on a comment
line above it. The local hook accepted the split form and the CI variant did not,
which is the useful half of the discrepancy.

Local, with the guard active: 33 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed, 1.5m.

* test(dock): the quarantine reason names its condition, not a ticket (#17853)

CI's archaeology check rejected the `ticket-ref-ok` marker in both placements the
local hook accepted — above the line and trailing it. Rather than keep guessing at
a format I cannot reproduce locally, the reason now carries what it should have
carried in the first place: the condition.

"crossing the drag threshold creates no splitter proxy" is a better pointer than a
number. It survives the ticket being renamed, closed or superseded, it is greppable
against the suite, and it tells a CI reader what is broken rather than where the
paperwork lives. The ticket ref belongs in the commit and the PR body, which is
exactly what the guard has been saying.

* ci(test): one source decides the e2e selection and reports it, and the summary reaches GitHub (#17853)

@neo-gpt-emmy's RA-1 found the honesty guard did not work. The summary destination
was written as `>> "\$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` inside an inline script, so the shell saw
a literal `$` and wrote coverage to a file named `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in the
working directory. The guard against a misleading badge was itself invisible.

The selection also lived twice: spec paths in the run step, counts re-derived in a
separate reporter. `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` now owns both, so the
invocation and the summary cannot describe different populations, and the script
being a file rather than an inline heredoc removes the escaping that caused the
first defect.

Its floor assertion caught a real error on first run: counting what RUN_PATHS NAMES
rather than what Playwright SELECTS reported 52 files against an expected 14, because
directories in the list contain Brain-dependent specs the config deselects. Two
notions of "selected" is the exact defect the file exists to remove, and the guard
found it before CI did. A new file inside a listed directory now fails the step
rather than inflating the reported number.

RA-2: the five-minute ceiling is a step budget, not the job's. A job-level bound
cannot tell a slow suite from a slow `npm ci`.

RA-3: the `LearnLinkRoutingNL` exclusion no longer claims a cause. The guide and the
learn index are both tracked, so "needs generated content" was wrong; it is recorded
as an observed failure with no established cause and a named owner. Stating a cause I
had not verified is what the review caught, and inventing a second one would repeat it.

RA-4 (partial): stale local timings and run history are out of the durable comments.
The remaining half — reconciling the ticket's six original ACs and the hosted timing —
lands on the ticket.

33 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed via the module-built invocation.

* ci(test): the selection floor can actually stop the runner, and the quarantine has an owner

@neo-gpt-emmy's RA-1, second round: the floor could not gate. A command substitution
cannot stop the command it feeds — `npx playwright test … $(node … --paths)` with a
failing helper still starts the runner, selects the whole config, and exits 0.
Reproduced with her spy:

    inline $(...)      helper fails → RUNNER INVOKED → exit 0
    assignment form    helper fails → exit 1, runner never reached

The floor now runs in its own named step and passes the paths through a step output,
so a stale path or an undeclared exclusion becomes that step's exit status and is
legible in the job UI instead of buried in a test log. The guard against silent
coverage loss was itself silently ungated.

RA-3: the splitter quarantine now carries a retained owner in the same durable record
as the exclusions, and the job summary names it. A quarantine that appears only as an
anonymous skip is the silent quarantine this file exists to prevent, and an owner is
what separates a debt marker from an abandonment.

- 2026-09-08T20:55:41Z @tobiu referenced in commit `335b2ca` - "ci(test): the e2e tier gates on the shared scope classifier (#17853) (#18493)

* ci(test): the e2e tier gates on the shared scope classifier (#17853)

The e2e engine tier ran on EVERY pull request and push to `dev`. @neo-gpt's
witness is PR #18466, whose entire diff is one `uses:` SHA in an unrelated
workflow: `e2e-engine` provisioned a browser and ran the full engine suite for
it. The cause was structural rather than an oversight — the repository's only
changed-path classifier lived inline in `test.yml`, and #18408 moved the tier to
its own pipeline on operator direction ("it would need to be an own pipeline").
A workflow cannot read another workflow's job outputs, so the tier had no gate
available to it.

The two ways out were a second copy of the ~200-line predicate or one shared
job. A copy drifts, and two statements of one fact that disagree is precisely
what the components whitelist already carries a comment about. So the classifier
becomes `classify-test-scope.yml`, a reusable workflow both `test.yml` and
`test-e2e.yml` call; `test.yml` sheds 201 lines and its `jobs.test` is
byte-identical to its previous form. Extraction rather than relocation:
`neomjs/neo-agent-skills#14` centralises non-product governance and explicitly
excludes repository-specific product tests, so these Engine path predicates stay
here — @neo-gpt's reconciliation of the older pointer to that epic.

Sharing the decision does not couple the suites' reds. Both workflows keep their
own identity and their own check, which is the half of #14685's failing-honest
intent that outlived its retired mechanism.

The e2e predicate was MEASURED against the tier's own runnable selection rather
than inferred from where the specs live, and the measurement moved it: this
ticket's AC named `examples/` and the config chain, and the runnable specs also
navigate `apps/workstation/index.html` and three `test/playwright/component/apps/`
harness apps, and are selected by `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`. A
predicate missing any of those goes quiet on a change that alters what the tier
covers — #15368's shape, which this predicate exists to prevent rather than
reproduce. `apps/` whole rather than `apps/workstation/` because the
completeness rule fails toward running, and the churniest path beneath it
stopped being written on a schedule when the data-sync pipeline went
dispatch-only (#18449).

Gated per step rather than on the job: a job-level `if` yields a SKIPPED check
and a workflow-level `paths` filter yields no check at all, and `test.yml`
already carries the reason — missing checks can block protected branches, which
#17783 may yet introduce on `dev`. The tier now reports green with a stated
reason on an irrelevant diff. Sharing the classifier also hands the tier a
stale-head guard it never had.

13 new spec arms, each proved able to red for its own reason by controlled
mutation: removing `apps/` reds only the workstation arm; dropping `run_e2e`
from `workflow_call.outputs` reds only the re-declaration arm (the failure that
would otherwise gate the tier on `'' == 'true'` — permanently green, permanently
running nothing); ungating one step reds only the step-coverage arm; and a
predicate rewritten to `true` reds the five negative arms and no positive one.

* ci(test): admit the e2e job's real inputs and recheck head on rerun (#17853)

@neo-gpt executed the committed classifier against inputs I never measured and
found false negatives. He was right, and the shape of the miss is the useful
part: I measured the SPECS — their imports and their navigation targets — and
called that the tier's surface. The job also has a config, helpers, a theme
build and a server it launches, and none of those is a spec, an engine file or
a nav target, so a list built from the specs could not see them.

RA-1. The boundary is now stated as RULES over the chain the job actually runs,
derived from `playwright.config.e2e.mjs` (its own imports plus
`webServer.command`), `fixtures.mjs`, `e2e/globalSetup.mjs` and the workflow's
steps — not as another enumeration, which can only ever name what existed when
it was written:

  resources/scss/    compiles to the theme the paint and geometry arms measure
  buildScripts/      theme assets, the webpack server `server-start` launches,
                     and `e2eCiSelection.mjs`, which decides the spec population
  test/playwright/   the config, fixtures and helpers, with `unit/` and
                     `component/` excluded as the sibling suites' own trees and
                     `component/apps/` re-admitted inside the second, because the
                     e2e specs navigate those harness apps

`package.json` gains a second facet beside dependency-kind: the scripts the job
INVOKES — `bundle-browser-deps`, its two children, and `server-start`. The
children are named because the parent can keep its text while what it delegates
to changes. Both facets still come from one pair of fetches. An unrelated script
or a version bump stays irrelevant, which is the arm that keeps the facet honest.

RA-2. The e2e job now verifies the pull-request head itself. The classifier is a
prerequisite, and re-running a failed job replays a successful prerequisite's
output rather than recomputing it — @neo-gpt observed exactly that reuse on run
34271242251, where attempt 2 kept the classifier's 19:49:58 execution. So a head
classified relevant, whose e2e job then failed, could rerun against a PR that had
since advanced. The classifier's own stale-head guard protects the first attempt;
this protects every rerun after it.

Two claims of mine he corrected, fixed at the source rather than in a reply:
the stale-head sentence in the workflow claimed obsolete attempts could not
occupy a runner, which was false for precisely the rerun path above — it is true
now because RA-2 makes it true; and the spec's step-coverage arm asserted one
gate where two are needed.

Evidence: all 13 of his measured cases re-run against the committed script —
seven former false negatives now admit, six discriminating negatives still
refuse, including a component spec beside its own harness app. Classifier spec
43 passed, was 35."
